pageCache.text:
Love, Learn, Live as One Community, Love, Respect, Trust
Welcome to Bisley Blue Coat CofE Primary School
As Interim Executive Headteacher, it is my absolute privilege to welcome you to Bisley Blue Coat Church of England Primary School, a truly special place nestled within the beautiful Stroud district of the Cotswolds.
At Bisley, our Christian vision of ‘Love, Learn, Live as One’ and Christian values of community, love, respect and trust are deeply embedded in daily life and guide everything we do. Love sits at the heart of our small school, reflecting Jesus' command to ‘love one another’. We pride ourselves on providing a safe, nurturing and supportive environment where every child's emotional, pastoral and spiritual needs are met with care, compassion and understanding. Respect shapes our relationships, ensuring that every child is valued, celebrated and included, while trust underpins the strong partnerships we build with families, staff and the wider community.
What makes Bisley truly unique, however, is our remarkable sense of community. We are proud of the small, close-knit village school we are, where relationships are built on kindness, mutual respect and a shared commitment to helping every child flourish. Strong links between pupils, families, staff, our parish and the wider village are woven into the fabric of our school, enabling us to truly live as one.
This spirit of togetherness is strengthened by our rich history, which dates back to 1732, making Bisley one of the oldest schools in Gloucestershire. Originally founded as a Blue Coat school, with children proudly wearing their traditional blue uniforms, we became a church school in 1863 under the guidance of Rev. Thomas Keble. His legacy of faith, service and commitment to education continues to inspire our work today.
This year sees Bisley Blue Coat continue its exciting interim partnership with the Heartwood Federation. As Executive Headteacher of Heartwood Federation, I am proud to support this collaboration, which places children firmly at the heart of all we do. Heartwood's vision aligns closely with Bisley's - both rooted in love, respect and a commitment to lifelong learning.
I warmly invite you to explore our website to discover more about our wonderful school. Whether you are a current family, a prospective parent or simply a friend of Bisley, thank you for taking the time to learn more about our thriving, historic and deeply caring Christian community.
Mrs Sarah Broadbent BEd, NASENCo, NPQELInterim Executive Headteacher
Click here to watch our 'Every Day is an Open Day' video
Noticeboard
Bisley Blue Coat Church of England School is a Voluntary Controlled School.
This means that we are a state school funded by the government through the Local Authority.
We are maintained (controlled) by the LA - Gloucestershire County Council.
Voluntary Controlled schools are also influenced by foundations or trusts, in our case this will be the Church of England.

pageCache.text:
Blossoms Pre-school
Blossoms pre-school is a school run pre-school.
We aim to offer places to children aged 3-4 years old.
The pre-school will be open for the standard school day from 8.45am to 3.15pm.
If you are interested in a place for your child, please see the admissions menu and send an application form to the school..
Contact Dawn Lane (School Business Manager) on admin@bisleybluecoat.gloucs.sch.uk
Blossoms Pre-school Opening April 2024
About Us
Blossoms is a school run pre-school located within Bisley Blue Coat CofE Primary.
Our goal is to support children’s learning and development from the age of 3 to 4 years in an environment that is supportive, nurturing, fun, stimulating and safe.
We can offer places for up to 8 children per day both funded and non-funded.
Aims
Our main priority at Blossoms is the happiness and emotional wellbeing of the children. In a warm and secure environment the child learns to relate to others, both children and adults. They learn to work and play alongside the other children and co-operate with them, gradually developing confidence, independence and the ability to use initiative.
Play is vitally important at this stage of a child’s development. It is from play that they gain experience to form their concepts and understanding of what they are learning.
Language is very important in our programme and the staff work with all children to encourage speech and purposeful conversation. They extend the vocabulary by talking and reading to them.
We aim to promote skills that they will later be taught when they move into Reception. The staff have a programme of activities to stimulate the children as they increase their capabilities. There is plenty of opprtunity to play and learn alongside our current Reception children.
Every child deserves the best possible start in life and support to fulfil their potential. A child’s experience in the early years has a major impact on their future life chances. A secure, safe and happy childhood is important in its own right, and it provides the foundation for children to make the most of their abilities and talents as they grow up. When parents choose to use early years services they want to know that provision will keep their children safe and help them to thrive. The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) is the framework that provides that assurance.
